blocks.text: The module documentation defines the defense-in-depth role, validation sequence, output limits, logging policy, and separation from session tools. Imports bring in concrete executors, path guards, shell outcomes, and logging.
blocks.title: Executor boundary and imports

blocks.text: Positive integer and number helpers reject invalid limits. Caps stores per-call size, timeout, result, deletion, and temporary-file bounds and validates them when constructed.
blocks.title: Caps and validation helpers

blocks.text: _state_dirs gathers M2C state locations defensively. ToolContext validates the project root, builds a denylist, selects caps, tracks seen files, and records an optional ripgrep path.
blocks.title: Protected state and tool context

blocks.text: ToolResult represents success or failure, bounded output, trust, local error code, duration, and optional shell exit status. to_payload excludes the local-only error code and emits the protocol result fields.
blocks.title: Tool result wire shape

blocks.text: ArgSpec describes type, requiredness, numeric bounds, and defaults. ARG_SPECS mirrors the supported file, search, and bash schemas; TOOLS maps names to concrete executors, while session-only tools are listed separately.
blocks.title: Argument specifications and dispatch tables

blocks.anchor: def _validate(name: str, args: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
blocks.text: _validate requires an object, rejects unknown and missing keys, enforces exact primitive types, checks integer ranges, and returns only accepted supplied arguments.
blocks.title: Closed argument validation

blocks.text: Helpers create stable failures, calculate elapsed milliseconds, log only non-sensitive counts and status, clamp oversized output, detect explicit call_env parameters, and normalize ToolOutcome trust and exit-code fields.
blocks.title: Failure, timing, logging, and outcome normalization

blocks.anchor: def run_tool(context: ToolContext, name: Any, args: Any, *, call_env: Any = None) -> ToolResult:
blocks.text: run_tool rejects session or unknown tools, validates arguments, invokes the selected executor, converts ToolError and unexpected exceptions to ToolResult, logs the call, and returns without raising ordinary tool failures.
blocks.title: Fail-closed tool execution

gotchas: ask_user and tasks are session tools and are rejected here.
Only executors explicitly declaring call_env receive the per-call environment.
Unexpected executor exceptions become content-free internal_error results.
how_it_works: Normalizes executor outputs and failures into ToolResult
purpose: This package is the executor boundary for tools proposed by the server after approval. It owns shared caps, project path context, argument validation, output clamping, trust labeling, error conversion, and privacy-limited call logging; the concrete executors live in sibling modules.
side_effects: filesystem and subprocess effects occur in delegated executors
